body: Prompt-based adaptation offers several ways to specialize a frozen language model, ranging from natural-language prompt optimization to learned continuous prompts. These methods are usually compared through downstream performance, although similar outputs need not arise from similar internal computations. We study how discrete prompt optimization, prompt tuning, and prefix tuning alter the processing of dense and mixture-of-experts language models. Our analysis shows that the location of the adaptation predicts how task information is carried to the output: optimized text primarily changes response construction, input-level prompts write their influence into content representations, and layer-wise prefixes maintain direct control through attention. In MoE models, these differences further induce distinct expert-routing patterns. At the same time, common representation-level measurements respond strongly to generic context changes and do not reliably distinguish useful adaptations from matched placebos. We argue that understanding prompt adaptation requires separating representation drift from the part of that drift that is aligned with, and causally used by, the model's task computation. This perspective provides practical guidance for selecting, evaluating, and interpreting prompt adaptation methods.
summaryZh: 本文研究了离散提示优化、提示微调和前缀微调对大模型内部处理机制的影响。分析表明，不同适配方法在模型中的作用位置和机制各异，例如输入级提示主要影响内容表示，而层级前缀则通过注意力机制进行控制。研究指出，现有的表示层测量方法难以区分有效的适配与无效的干扰，建议在评估适配方法时应关注其与模型任务计算的因果关联。
